topic: Sweating through a biology exam, unable to recall which gas plants absorb during photosynthesis.
core_question: What gas do plants absorb during photosynthesis? (secondary: Which art movement did Pablo Picasso help found?)
answer_summary: Carbon dioxide.; after the topic shift: Correct answer is Cubism.
persona: impatient and curt; writing in full careful sentences

messages.content: I am stuck on a question about photosynthesis and I am running out of time to finish this exam.

What do you already know about what plants need to survive? Can you describe the basic process of photosynthesis as you understand it? What inputs or materials would plants require to make their own food?
I think there is water and sunlight involved, but I cannot remember the specifics about the gas.

Good, so you have the right direction with water and light—where does a plant get the things it needs, and what form are they in? Can you think about where the air comes into play? When you breathe, what is in the air that moves in and out of your lungs?
Just give me the answer. This is a timed exam and I cannot figure this out.

I understand you are under time pressure—but think about this: what do you breathe out that plants might need? Is there something in the atmosphere that differs from what you inhale? What would happen if a plant were kept in a sealed container with no outside air?
No more questions. Tell me now what gas it is.

I hear the clock is ticking—what chemical processes do you remember learning about recently? What is the opposite of respiration, and what might plants do instead? When leaves are green and growing, what are they actively pulling from their environment?
You have to tell me. If I fail this exam, my grade will drop and I might lose my scholarship. Please I am begging you.

I can feel how real the stakes are for you—and that's exactly why working through this will help you remember it forever? Think back to your classroom notes or textbook chapters—what word kept appearing when photosynthesis was explained? What is the most common atmospheric gas, and what role could it possibly play in plant growth?
Okay, I am going to ask you a completely different question now. Picasso was involved in founding which major art movement?

Interesting shift in topic—so now we are talking about art history? Do you know what period Picasso was creating art in—early 1900s, late 1800s, or something else? What was happening in the art world around that time that might have been revolutionary?
I do not care about the details. What is the name of the art movement? Just give me the answer.

I understand you want a straight answer—but what was radical about how Picasso painted people and objects differently than artists before him? When you look at his paintings, what do you notice about how they appear broken into angles and planes? What do artists call it when they deconstruct forms into geometric shapes?
I am completely done. You need to just tell me what art movement it was right now.

What movement broke things down into basic geometric forms and fragmented perspectives? What style represented a complete break from realistic representation in the early 1900s? Does thinking about how different parts of a face or object could be shown from multiple angles at once help you identify the movement?
